title: Canonical orbit-bundle base change and specialized norm-coordinate sections
statement: Let $F\subset E$ be fields [def-weil-field], let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ be a scheme over $F$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-base-change], let $G$ be a finite group acting by $F$-automorphisms $\rho_g$, and let $L$ be an $\mathcal O_C$-module. Use normalized module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the orbit bundle and norm [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm], the canonical pullback tensor and power comparisons [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison], and powers of module isomorphisms [def-sfb-tensor-power-pullback-comparisons]. For any scheme morphism $q:Y\to X$, families $\alpha_g\in\operatorname{Aut}(X)$, $\beta_g\in\operatorname{Aut}(Y)$ with $q\circ\beta_g=\alpha_g\circ q$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $A$, define $q^*T_\alpha(A,\ell)\simeq T_\beta(q^*A,\ell)$ recursively on a finite list $\ell$: on the empty list use the unit comparison; on $g::\ell$ distribute pullback over the tensor, identify $q^*\alpha_g^*A\simeq\beta_g^*q^*A$ using normalized pullback composition and the commuting square, and tensor with the recursive tail comparison. Write $\pi:C_E\to C$, $p:C_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ for the base-change projections, and $\rho_{E,g}$ for the base-changed automorphisms. Fix $n\in\mathbb N$, a finite index set $I$, and any family $b_i\in\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$. Put $P=\mathbb A_F^{I\times\{0,1\}}$ with coordinates $x_{i,j}$. For any scheme morphism $z:\operatorname{Spec}E\to P$, define the coordinate section indexed by $j$ to be the image of $\sum_i p^*(z^*x_{i,j})\,\pi^*b_i$ under the fixed comparison $\pi^*(L^{\otimes n})\simeq(\pi^*L)^{\otimes n}$. Define the specialized norm pair in $\Gamma(C_E,(\pi^*B_\rho(L))^{\otimes n})$ by taking the norms of these two coordinate sections for $\rho_E$ and $\pi^*L$, then applying the inverse of the nth tensor power of the displayed recursive orbit-bundle base-change comparison. No invertibility, ampleness, smoothness, generation, basis, or faithfulness is assumed. The constructions themselves are defined for arbitrary $z$; applications to $E$-valued $F$-points additionally require $z$ to be over $F$.

      pencilTranslateTensor β ((tensorPullback f).obj L) l
